clue.text: Healthy state of Ulysses' character

blocks.note: first meaning: the glow of health and vigour, as in the flush of youth
second meaning: Leopold, the hero of James Joyce's novel Ulysses

explanation.surface: A reader asks whether the Greek hero Ulysses was in sound moral health.
explanation.walkthrough: Ulysses here is Joyce's novel, not the Greek hero, and its central figure is Leopold Bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloom names a fresh, flourishing condition, and also the surname of the Dublin advertising canvasser at the centre of Joyce's book.

clue.text: Yacht copper was impressed with

blocks.note: first meaning: the royal yacht of the British monarch
second meaning: the seated figure stamped on the British penny

explanation.surface: A police officer was much taken with a sailing boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman but is a copper coin, and 'impressed' means stamped. Britannia appeared on British pennies for centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: HMY Britannia was the royal yacht from 1954, and the helmeted female figure symbolising Britain was struck onto penny coins.

clue.text: Record error derisively - double entry system's what you need

indicators.note: a double entry is one item written in twice, so the same run of letters sits within the clue's words two times over

blocks.note: the letters run from the middle of Record into the start of error
surface padding that also holds the second copy: the letters run again from the end of error into this word

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper sneers at a mistake in the ledger and recommends proper double-entry accounting.
explanation.walkthrough: Double-entry bookkeeping is the accounting method, but here it says the answer is entered twice: once across 'Record error' and once across 'error derisively'.
explanation.definitionFit: Order means a methodical arrangement or regular system, the tidiness a muddled set of accounts lacks.

clue.text: Belligerent and stingy type, in the main

blocks.note: first meaning: a warship, an armed fighting vessel
second meaning: the Portuguese ..., a stinging jellyfish-like creature of the open sea

explanation.surface: Someone quarrelsome and mean with money, for the most part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stingy' means having a sting, not mean, and 'the main' is the sea, not 'mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: A man-of-war is an armed sailing warship, a fighter; the Portuguese man-of-war is a venomous floating colony found in ocean waters.

clue.text: Ambitious type up with the lark?

blocks.note: first meaning: a person set on rising fast in a career
second meaning, playful: a bird soaring up there alongside the lark

explanation.surface: The go-getter is an early riser, out of bed at dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up with the lark' is the idiom for rising very early; read literally, it is something flying high in the sky beside the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A careerist with lofty goals is called a high-flier, and a bird or plane cruising at altitude literally is one.

clue.text: Entertain large crowd

blocks.note: first meaning: to receive guests
second meaning: a great number

explanation.surface: Put on a show for a big audience.
explanation.definitionFit: To host is to have people round as guests, and a host is also a multitude or great throng of people.

clue.text: Achievements of those who don't miss a trick

definitions.text: Achievements of those who don't miss a trick

blocks.clueFragment: those who don't miss a trick
blocks.note: surface reading: sharp, observant people who notice everything

blocks.clueFragment: Achievements of those who don't miss a trick
blocks.note: setter's reading: bridge partners who win every one of the thirteen tricks in a hand

explanation.surface: The successes of shrewd, alert people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not miss a trick' is the idiom for being sharp, but at bridge it means taking every trick.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, bidding and making all thirteen tricks of a deal is the top contract, the ultimate feat at the card table.

clue.text: Eg two or three of what precedes or follows this

definitions.text: Eg two or three of what precedes or follows this

blocks.note: surface reading: neighbouring items in some sequence
setter's reading: two and three both divide exactly into the number in brackets after the clue

explanation.surface: A puzzle about two or three items in a sequence before or after this one.
explanation.walkthrough: The number that follows 'this' is the enumeration (6), and 2 and 3 multiply to make it.
explanation.definitionFit: In arithmetic a factor is a whole number dividing exactly into another; two and three divide six evenly.

clue.text: In an instant, abandon a lover

blocks.note: taken as written
an instant is a moment, a MO, with the article as A
to rat is to desert, as rats leave a sinking ship
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone leaves their sweetheart in the blink of an eye.
explanation.walkthrough: MO is British informal for a moment, as in 'half a mo'.
explanation.definitionFit: An inamorata is a woman who is someone's sweetheart or beloved, the Italian word for a female lover.

clue.text: Why you are said to hold thousands up in game

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words count for their sound as single letters
holding something means wrapping round it
in a down clue, going up means reading from the bottom to the top

blocks.note: the letter whose name is pronounced like the question word
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, doubled for the plural
two letters spoken like the two words, text-message style

explanation.surface: A player wonders aloud why someone is holding up thousands in the middle of a card game.
explanation.walkthrough: Letters standing for words is text-message style: Y for why, U for you, R for are. M is the Roman thousand.
explanation.definitionFit: Rummy is a card game in which players collect sets and runs of cards, a standard family pastime.

clue.text: Units seen in one Eastern country or another

indicators.note: something seen in a place sits inside it, so one word goes within the other

blocks.note: a country of the East
units are single things, ones

explanation.surface: A traveller notices the same measuring units used in one Asian nation and the next.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' is the whole definition: it means a second Eastern country, distinct from the one in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Asian archipelago republic is a second Eastern nation, the 'another' that follows 'one Eastern country'.

clue.text: Bad spelling, perhaps, in Daily Mail's leader

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the front letter of the paper's name is wanted

blocks.note: a daily is a cleaning woman who comes in each day, also called a char
the opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: A newspaper editorial is criticised for its poor spelling.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Mail is a British newspaper and a leader is its editorial, but here 'Daily' is a cleaner (a char, in British usage). 'Bad spelling' is not misspelling but a magic spell, possibly a wicked one.
explanation.definitionFit: A charm is an incantation or spell, and one cast to harm would be a bad piece of spelling in the witch's sense.

clue.text: An import subject to current control

blocks.note: the article as a single letter
the import of a speech is its drift, its general meaning

explanation.surface: Imported goods are bound by the trade regulations now in force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present-day' but means a flow of water; 'import' is not trade goods but meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is loose and unsteered goes wherever the flow of water carries it, so it is governed by the current.

clue.text: Assemble, that is, goodly collection of beliefs

indicators.note: to assemble is to put parts together into a new whole, so the letters are built up afresh

blocks.note: i.e. is the abbreviation for that is
taken as written

explanation.surface: A call to gather a sizeable body of convictions together.
explanation.definitionFit: An ideology is a system of ideas and principles, the set of convictions behind a politics or worldview.

clue.text: Bankrupted by no turnover in strike action

indicators.note: turning something over flips it so it runs the other way
in puts one string inside another

blocks.note: the opening half of STROKE, a strike or blow
taken as written
the rest of STROKE, which wraps round the turned words

explanation.surface: A company was ruined because nobody's turnover held up during an industrial dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turnover' and 'strike action' sound like business and trade unions; here they mean reversal and a stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony-broke is British informal for having no money at all, completely penniless, which is how a bankrupt ends up.

clue.text: Spanish area one found in English city

indicators.note: a thing found in another is sitting inside it

blocks.note: the city on the Tyne in north-east England
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Part of Spain turns up, oddly, inside an English town.
explanation.walkthrough: I slips into NEWCASTLE between its T and L. New Castile was a historic region of central Spain around Madrid.
explanation.definitionFit: New Castile is the old name for the central Spanish region around Toledo and Madrid, a historic part of the country.

clue.text: Water supply exhausted, not squandered

blocks.note: a well supplies water
spent means used up, worn out

explanation.surface: The water supply has run dry, though none of it was wasted.
explanation.definitionFit: Money or time used wisely and to good purpose is described as well spent, the opposite of wasted.

clue.text: Manage without Dutch or German composer

blocks.note: first meaning: to live as a bachelor, getting by with no wife
second meaning: Johann Sebastian, the Baroque master

explanation.surface: Choosing between Dutch and German composers when one must do without the Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like the nationality, but 'my old Dutch' is Cockney slang for a wife (from duchess). To bach, or batch, is to keep house as a bachelor.
explanation.definitionFit: Batching or baching means a single man fending for himself with no spouse; separately, the surname of the composer of the Brandenburg Concertos.

clue.text: Hardy's novel about a very foolish nymph

indicators.note: novel means new and original, so the name's letters take a new form
about means going round, so one piece surrounds another

blocks.note: the novelist's surname rearranged, its first part
taken as written
mad is wildly foolish
the rest of the rearranged surname

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy novel tells of a silly woodland spirit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy's novel' looks like a book title, but novel means the surname's letters are reshuffled, then split round A MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth a hamadryad is a tree nymph whose life is bound to one particular tree.

clue.text: They can never make better profit

definitions.text: They can never make better profit

blocks.clueFragment: They can never make better profit
blocks.note: surface reading: businesses that can never improve their earnings
setter's reading: horses that never finish placed, so a punter, the better, never collects on them

explanation.surface: Firms that have no hope of raising their returns.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' is not 'improved' but a person who bets. An also-ran is a horse that finishes outside the places.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, an also-ran is a runner that finishes unplaced, so anyone backing it loses the stake.

clue.text: Confederate may be loyal, nonetheless

indicators.note: split as none-less, it asks for the nothing-shaped letter to be dropped
what the letters may be is a different arrangement of them

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Confederate soldier might stay faithful in spite of everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Take O, the letter shaped like nought, out of LOYAL and rearrange the rest. 'Confederate' suggests the American Civil War but is just a partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A confederate is an associate joined with others in a common cause, which is what an ally is.

clue.text: Fields of honour for Napoleon's troops

definitions.text: Fields of honour for Napoleon's troops

blocks.clueFragment: Fields of honour for Napoleon's troops
blocks.note: surface reading: the battlefields where the French emperor's army fought with glory
setter's reading: Napoleon is the pig who rules in Orwell's fable, and his troops are the beasts on the farm

explanation.surface: The glorious battlefields of the Napoleonic Wars, where the Grande Armée won renown.
explanation.walkthrough: Napoleon is the boar who seizes power in George Orwell's 1945 novel, so his fields are those of the farm the animals take over.
explanation.definitionFit: Orwell's satire is set on a farm run by its livestock under the pig Napoleon, so its fields belong to his followers.

clue.text: Project for one in Kipling's book company

blocks.note: first meaning: to overhang, as beetling brows or cliffs jut out
second meaning: one of the three schoolboys in Kipling's Stalky & Co

explanation.surface: A publishing company's plan for an author involved in a Kipling book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Company' points to the title Stalky & Co, whose trio is Stalky, M'Turk and Beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: To beetle is to jut out or overhang; Beetle is also the schoolboy nickname of a character based on Kipling himself.

clue.text: Successful candidate close to priest or Levite

blocks.note: one who passes an exam
by means near, as in close by

explanation.surface: A winning applicant finds themself near a clergyman or a temple official.
explanation.walkthrough: In the parable of the Good Samaritan, a priest and a Levite each see the wounded man and pass by on the other side.
explanation.definitionFit: Both religious men in the Gospel story walk past without helping, so each is literally someone going past.

clue.text: Chanteuse not loud? No, by no means

indicators.note: by no means says the singer must lack something, the loud mark musicians write as a single letter

blocks.note: Edith Piaf, the great French singer
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked whether a nightclub singer is quiet, the reply is a firm negative.
explanation.walkthrough: F is the musical mark forte, loud; Piaf loses it. Piano is the Italian musical direction to play softly.
explanation.definitionFit: In musical notation, piano instructs the performer to play softly, the opposite of forte.

clue.text: Could conscience make anyone like this dramatist?

definitions.text: Could conscience make anyone like this

blocks.clueFragment: Could conscience make anyone like this
blocks.note: first meaning: Hamlet says conscience does make ... of us all
second meaning: Noël, the English playwright of Private Lives

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a guilty conscience could turn a person into a playwright.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half quotes Hamlet's soliloquy: 'Thus conscience does make cowards of us all'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's line says scruples turn people timid and fearful; separately, the surname of the witty twentieth-century English playwright Noël.

clue.text: Shrink from following out Alfred's letters

indicators.note: out means removed, so the letter standing for following is taken away
the remaining letters are used as a set, rearranged rather than in their order

blocks.note: f. is the abbreviation for following, as in page references
taken as written

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist backs away after reading someone's correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: Shrink is slang for a psychiatrist; the shrink here is Alfred Adler, whose first name supplies his surname's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Adler was an Austrian psychotherapist, founder of individual psychology, and so a 'shrink' in the slang sense.

clue.text: Gardener shows a way to stem flower

blocks.note: taken as written
a flower is something that flows, a river, and a dam holds it back

explanation.surface: A horticulturist demonstrates a technique for cutting flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' means a river (it flows), and 'stem' means hold back, not cut a stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: Genesis puts Adam in the Garden of Eden to tend and keep it, making him the first gardener.

clue.text: Skilful predecessors of B.E.F. training

blocks.note: the letter coming just before each of B, E and F in the alphabet
PT is physical training

explanation.surface: Expert forerunners of the British Expeditionary Force are drilled.
explanation.walkthrough: B.E.F. looks like the British Expeditionary Force of the World Wars, but it is three separate letters, each stepped back one place in the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: An adept person is highly proficient, expert at something, which is to say skilful.

clue.text: Early defence in court

blocks.note: early as in old, from former times
a bailey is the outer wall or courtyard of a castle's defences

explanation.surface: A barrister lays out the defence case at the start of a trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The Old Bailey is the popular name for London's Central Criminal Court. 'Defence' is not a lawyer's case but castle fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Central Criminal Court, where major English criminal trials are heard, is universally known by this name.

clue.text: Right place for some gymnastic exercises

blocks.note: first meaning: on the right track, as a plane follows a radio guide beam
second meaning: performing on the balance apparatus

explanation.surface: The proper spot to do gymnastics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right place' reads as one phrase, but 'Right' stands alone as the first meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom comes from aircraft guided by radio signals, meaning correct; literally it is where a gymnast stands on the balance apparatus.

clue.text: Fine thing to play with bow and arrows? Just the reverse

definitions.text: Fine thing to play with bow

indicators.note: the reverse of a word is that word read from its end back to its start

blocks.note: darts are small arrows thrown at a board

explanation.surface: Archery gear: a pleasant toy is a bow and arrows, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bow and arrows' looks like one archery set; the bow belongs with the fiddle, and the arrows are the wordplay. A Strad is a Stradivarius violin.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stradivarius violin is a superb instrument played with a bow, and Strad is its common short name.
